name: Nepal
summary: Two stacked crimson pennants with a blue border, a white moon in the upper one and a white sun in the lower. It is the only non-rectangular national flag, and its constitution sets out its construction as a step-by-step geometric procedure.
origin: Triangular pennants have flown over the Indian subcontinent and Himalayas for centuries. The double pennant was in use well before the 20th century; older versions drew the sun and moon with human faces.

On 16 December 1962 a new constitution standardised the flag, removed the faces from the sun and moon and set out a detailed geometric construction. The interim constitution of 2007 and the Constitution of Nepal of 2015 keep the same flag and construction in Schedule 1.

colors.name: Crimson
colors.meaning: Nepal's national colour and the colour of the rhododendron, the national flower; also read as bravery.

symbols.name: Two pennants
symbols.description: Two overlapping right-angled triangles, the upper smaller, forming a double pennant.
symbols.meaning: Often said to stand for the Himalayas, or for Hinduism and Buddhism, the country's two main religions.

symbols.name: Moon
symbols.description: A white crescent with eight rays in the upper pennant.
symbols.meaning: The hope that Nepal will last as long as the sun and moon; also read as the calm, cool temperament of the Nepali people.

symbols.name: Sun
symbols.description: A twelve-rayed white sun in the lower pennant.
symbols.meaning: The hope for the nation's permanence; also read as fierce resolve and the heat of the lowlands.

history.label: Traditional double pennant
history.note: The sun and moon were drawn with human faces.

history.label: Standardised flag
history.note: Faces removed and geometry fixed by the 1962 constitution.

facts: Schedule 1 of the Constitution gives numbered geometric steps for drawing the flag; its proportions involve an irrational number, roughly 1:1.2190.
It is the only national flag that is not a rectangle. Ohio's swallowtail is the only non-rectangular US state flag.
Its national colour, crimson, is also the colour of the rhododendron.
clues: The only national flag that is not a rectangle.
Two stacked crimson pennants with a blue border.
A white moon above and a white sun below.
Its constitution gives step-by-step geometric instructions for drawing it.
